Learning with videos

Pros

Cheap or free.
You can practice whenever you want.
Videos are excellent for understanding what a technique should look like.
Great for reinforcing things you've already learned from an instructor.

Cons

You can't easily tell what you're doing wrong.
Some swimming mistakes are subtle but significantly affect efficiency.
It's harder to learn breathing and water confidence without someone observing you.
Videos can't adapt to your specific fear, mobility, coordination, or skill level.
What I'd recommend

Best option: combine them.

Take private lessons for the fundamentals—perhaps 4–8 lessons—and practice independently between lessons. Use videos afterward to reinforce what your instructor taught you.

For example:

Lesson → practice on your own → watch a relevant video → practice again → next lesson for correction.

If you're already comfortable in deep water and can swim several lengths, you can probably get a lot more mileage from self-learning. But if you're starting from zero or aren't comfortable putting your face underwater, I'd strongly favor private instruction first.

Before a private swim lesson at your house, I’d have these ready:

🩱 Proper swimwear and a towel
🩴 Flip-flops/water shoes if the pool deck is hot or slippery
🥤 Water bottle for before/after the lesson
🧴 Sunscreen if the lesson is outdoors
🥽 Goggles if you normally use them
🏊 Any swim equipment your instructor requested (kickboard, fins, pull buoy, etc.)
🌡️ A comfortable pool temperature and a clean, accessible pool
🧹 Clear the pool area of toys, floats, furniture, or anything that could get in the way
🚿 Easy access to the bathroom/changing area
🧑‍🏫 A spot for the instructor to enter and get changed, if applicable
📱 Your phone nearby in case you need to contact the instructor, but safely out of the wet area

If it’s a child’s lesson, I’d also have them use the bathroom beforehand, bring a warm change of clothes, and have a snack ready for afterward.
